blogs.title: Deference to Entry, Not Service: How *Pacito* Distinguishes Presidential Power in Immigration Admissions from Mandatory Resettlement Duties
blogs.description: This analysis examines the Ninth Circuit's application of *Trump v. Hawaii* deference to distinguish between the President's broad authority under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f) to suspend refugee admissions, and the statutory obligations under the Refugee Act regarding domestic resettlement services. The post explores the court's reasoning on why the suspension of entry admissions is presumptively valid pending finding, while rejecting the broad deference granted regarding the administrative mandate to provide reception and placement services for those already admitted.

blogs.title: Statutory Mandates or Administrative Permits? A Breakdown of the *Pacito v. Trump* Debate over 8 U.S.C. § 1522
blogs.description: Focusing on the Ninth Circuit's partial decision to reinstate cooperative agreements for refugee services, this post dissects the textual argument over whether 8 U.S.C. § 1522 imposes a mandatory duty on the executive branch ('shall') or is merely a discretionary authorization. By contrasting the majority's reading of the 'Conditions and Considerations' subsection with Judge Lee's dissent that frames the statute as a menu of options available when appropriated, the article analyzes the broader implications for administrative law and fiscal implementation in immigration contexts.

blogs.title: Staying the Hand of Discretion: How the *Pacito* Stay Order Employs *Nken v. Holder* Standards in a Humanitarian Crisis
blogs.description: This post analyzes the procedural mechanics of the Ninth Circuit's stay pending appeal in *Pacito*, specifically how the court applied the *Nken v. Holder* four-factor test amidst competing humanitarian interests and urgent budget cuts. It details how the court's failure to immediately intervene on the defense of the reservation's rights was balanced against the government's emergency motion, and how the order stabilized the refugee enrollment process while leaving the underlying merits open to full review in due course.
